1#main: The law of ohel — how it brings impurity. In it are 6 seifim. It is forbidden for a kohen to enter under an ohel with the dead beneath it, even if it is very large, even into another house or another upper story opened to that house, through an opening of a tefach by a tefach and a window to that house forever; and if he sealed the opening, it is permitted for him to enter another house, for the sealing interposes {Rama: even if not nullified to remain there forever; and all this when he sealed the entire opening; but if he did not seal the entire opening, only part less than a tefach — if they placed it to remain forever, it diminishes and interposes before the impurity that it not pass; and if not, it does not diminish; and anything that receives impurity does not interpose before impurity (Hagahot Alfasi ch. Bnei HaIr and laws of impurity for Rif, Ramban, Rosh, and Mordechai beginning of ch. Lo Yachpor); and sealing in a window is not called sealing unless it can stand without support (same there).}
2#main: An opening between house and upper story without an opening of a tefach and an olive of the dead below in the house opposite the opening — the house is pure and the upper story impure.
3#main: Two rooms opened to a house, and in each half an olive of the dead and their doors locked — the house is impure and they are pure; and if opened, they too are impure.
4#main: A courtyard surrounded by projections and porticoes and impurity in one of the houses — if all openings and windows of the houses are locked, impurity goes out under the projections and porticoes {Rama: (and the reason is since ultimately impurity will go out that way, we view it as if it already went out; therefore some are stringent for kohanim to walk through the city gate from which the dead will ultimately go out (Piskei Maharai siman 25 and Kol Bo); and some permit (there citing some authorities); and one who is lenient does not lose where they did not practice to be stringent)}; and if a window or opening opened on the other side and those on the courtyard side are all locked, impurity does not go out under the projections; and if one of them also opened toward the projections, impurity goes out from the house under the projections; and likewise if impurity is under the projections, it enters from beneath them into the house; therefore roofs projecting outward above the doorways of houses and impurity in one of the houses — all houses whose doorways are open are impure: {Rama: Two roofs that do not touch each other — even if less than three between them, they are not joined for impurity, for we do not say lavud to be stringent (Mahariu in his rulings); and if one was above the other, even if not touching, we say chavot rami — as if touching (Nimmukei Yosef laws of impurity for Rif); kohanim cannot compel the dead's relatives to remove the dead so they may enter their houses except where it is customary to remove all dead (responsum of Maharil siman 65).}
5#main: It is forbidden to approach within four amot of the dead or of a grave — in what case? When the grave is not defined by partitions ten tefachim high; but if defined by partitions ten tefachim high or in a ditch ten tefachim deep, one need not distance except four tefachim {Rama: (and a kohen may stand beside a house with a dead inside and touch its walls, provided nothing shelters over him) (responsum of Rashba siman 336).}
6#main: A dead person placed in a ship — if it is small so it sways when one steps in it, a kohen is forbidden to enter it.
